'''Pierre Henry John Young''' (12 June 1926 – 4 August 1985) was a British mathematician, of French heritage, who was in charge, during the 1960s, of the engine development for [[Concorde]].

==Early life==
He was born in France, speaking French. He attended [[Lycée Condorcet]], and school in England from 1938, being evacuated to [[Herefordshire]].

At [[Trinity College, Cambridge]] he studied Maths.<ref>''Times'' obituary Wednesday August 7, 1985, page 12</ref> Whilst at Cambridge, his knowledge of the French language was given to the BBC foreign language service, for coded messages to the French Resistance.

==Career==
He joined Bristol Siddeley in 1949, and in
1959 he became assistant chief engineer.

===Concorde engine===
He was the head of Concorde engine programme from 1962.<ref>''Bristol Evening Post'' Wednesday 20 December 1967, page 2</ref> This was taken over by Rolls-Royce from 1966. His knowledge of the French language helped the two teams socialise, and work. He understood the 'volatile French temperament'.

On Wednesday 3 April 1969, he appeared on 'The Change Makers' on BBC1 at 10.50pm.<ref>''Western Daily Press'' Friday 3 January 1969, page 4</ref>
<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20230205163356/https://genome.ch.bbc.co.uk/40a21ac6c9014b9c9b59b1308298bb7a The Change Makers January 1969]</ref>

On 2 March 1969, he attended the first flight of Concorde, in France.,<ref>''Bristol Evening Post'' Monday 3 March 1969, page 16</ref> with his deputy, [[Peter Calder]].

By the early 1970s, he was Technical Director of the Bristol Engine Division of Rolls-Royce. He gave a talk about Concorde on Wednesday 3 May 1972 at the Bristol branch of the [[Royal Aeronautical Society]].<ref>''Bristol Evening Post'' Thursday 4 May 1972, page 13</ref>
In February 1975 he became deputy technical director of Rolls-Royce.<ref>''Nottingham Evening Post'' Thursday 27 February 1975, page 8</ref>

He was featured on the 'Faster than the Sun' documentary on BBC1 on Wednesday 13 April 1983, following Speedbird 193 from London, with Captain [[Brian Walpole]] and [[Christopher Orlebar]], passing by Nova Scotia and [[Nantucket]].<ref>
[https://web.archive.org/web/20230205163357/https://genome.ch.bbc.co.uk/930351d45d894bcff897b1ff97867f2a Faster than the Sun 1983]</ref><ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20230205163357/https://www2.bfi.org.uk/films-tv-people/4ce2b6e6b1950 BFI 1983]</ref>

He received the RAeS Gold medal in 1984.

==Personal life==
He married Lily Irene Cahn (German nationality, from [[Fürth]] in northern Bavaria, 14 July 1928- 4 January 1990) in 1953; her elder brother was [[Robert W. Cahn]] FRS, and her nephew is Sir [[Andrew Cahn]].

His son, Thomas, and daughter, Michele, both attended the University of Cambridge.

He went on holidays, climbing in the Alps. Twice a week he would put on his shorts, and jog around [[The Downs, Bristol]]. He lived on Rockleaze Avenue in [[Sneyd Park]], near [[Stoke Bishop]].<ref>''Western Daily Press'' 3 March 1969, page 27</ref><ref>''Bristol Evening Post'' Monday 3 March 1969, page 42</ref>
His memorial service was on 20 February 1986 at St Peter's church in [[Filton]], attended by his wife Irène.<ref>''Bristol Evening Post'' Friday 21 February 1986, page 14</ref>
